verification_report.summary:
The full supplement is correct under the stated hypotheses and expressly accepted prerequisites. All assertions and deductions were checked in textual order, with 17 detailed statement records and 8 reference records. The weighted norm is nondegenerate, keeps the continuous weight separate from the multiplier-ideal selector, and gives genuine theta-psh U_m with analytic singularity type whenever N_m>0.

The Jacobian order-loss lemma has the correct normalization. The supplied SGPT source and the author's public [SGPT, section 1.4](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT2.pdf#page=35) use nu(log|z|^2)=1 and multiplier weights exp(-u). Change of variables makes |(g o pi)J_pi|^2 exp(-m phi o pi) integrable. Its first nonzero homogeneous Taylor term gives a positive spherical lower bound of order r^(2k). Radial integrability requires k+n>m delta for every delta<nu(phi o pi,y), hence k+n>=m nu(phi o pi,y). Subtracting the Jacobian order gives exactly n+ord_y J_pi. Taking the minimum of the section orders and dividing by m proves the asserted U_m estimate.

The new local modification L1-continuity proof is valid independently of the compact-modification lemma. Downstairs L1 convergence gives local uniform upper bounds; pullback and smooth correction give a common local psh class upstairs. Every connected coordinate region meets the biholomorphic complement of the exceptional locus. Convergence there excludes collapse to -infinity and identifies every cluster limit. The exceptional locus has volume zero, so canonical representatives and uniqueness give convergence of the whole sequence locally upstairs.

The single-section extremal evaluation formula and Bernstein-Markov inequality give exactly delta_m,epsilon=2epsilon+2log(C_epsilon)/m, with no N_m factor. The compact-obstacle lemma applies to all theta-psh functions and supplies a uniform global upper bound after subtracting delta. The exact trace integral equals N_m>=1; probability normalization therefore gives sup_X U_m>=min_K w. These two bounds and normalized compactness yield relative L1 compactness with genuine limits.

For each fixed local modification and point, upstairs L1 convergence and Lelong semicontinuity retain nu(U o pi,y)>=nu(phi o pi,y), since its fixed Jacobian error divided by m tends to zero. The same convergent subsequence works for every choice, without an uncountable diagonal extraction or a global extension of local modifications. The accepted local criterion then gives I(lambda U) contained in I(lambda phi) for every positive real lambda.

The obstacle argument is correct on thin compact sets. Minimal-singularity domination a<=V_theta+sup_X a implies a preceq_I V_theta for every theta-psh a, so G=E_theta,K[V_theta]_I(w) is unconstrained. Maximality gives U_m<=G+delta globally. Passing through an almost-everywhere L1 subsequence and canonical representatives, then letting epsilon decrease to zero, gives U<=G everywhere. Since G<=w quasi-everywhere on K, U satisfies the obstacle. Together with its ideal order this makes U a competitor for E_theta,K[phi]_I(w). No pointwise L1 convergence on K is assumed.

Moving-point Hartogs and compactness give the regularized upper-limit inequality everywhere, including poles of the envelope. Empty-space terms contribute only -infinity. If only finitely many spaces are nonzero, the sequence is eventually identically -infinity and so is its regularized limsup; the completely empty family is also covered.

Dependency status: partial_envelope_calculus_01 is completed with verdict correct. Its actual obstacle lemma, genuine largest-member theorem with a quasi-everywhere obstacle, and translation statement match every use here. This bounded audit imports that expressly accepted result. The finite-kernel prerequisites also have the stated completed correct audit. No Kahlerness, projectivity, mass positivity, bounded mass property, global generation, quotient asymptotic, lower convergence, or kernel-measure asymptotic is used or inferred.
